title: P2.15a Bound runtime handshake attempts
description: Objective: bound the existing runtime GET /bootstrap and POST /session/pair handshake without weakening its one-time-token or fail-closed rules. Deliverable: the current dirty live-handshake implementation accepts a caller cancellation signal plus a defaulted per-request deadline, ignores late answers, and preserves safe daemon code/layer tokens inside the existing local refusal detail. Not in scope: board-feed lifecycle, React shell state, retry UI, live-config vocabulary changes, or reverting any foreign Control Room WIP. Exact verification: `pnpm exec vitest run apps/control-room/src/live/live-handshake.test.ts` with exit 0 and nonzero Test Files/Tests lines.
definitionOfDone: Current-byte test measurement records that both production fetch calls lack signals/deadlines at claim time, while the existing healthy bootstrap/pair path and secret-exclusion assertions are preserved.

HandshakeInput supports an optional caller AbortSignal and requestTimeoutMs defaulting to 15000; bootstrap and pairing each receive a fresh deadline composed with caller cancellation, and all listeners/resources are released after settlement.

A timeout or external abort before bootstrap returns exactly LIVE_BOOTSTRAP_UNAVAILABLE and never calls pairing; a timeout or abort during pairing returns exactly LIVE_PAIRING_REFUSED, and no late response can later produce an ok setup.

Non-2xx daemon bodies preserve only validated non-secret code/layer tokens in the existing refusal detail when supplied; pairing tokens, credentials, arbitrary body fields, URLs, and raw errors are never echoed.

Focused tests cover success, bootstrap timeout/abort, pairing timeout/abort, late resolve, one-call/two-call counts, and a mutation removing the production signal/late-settlement guard reds the named assertion; the exact verification command exits 0 with nonzero counts.

implementationPlan.description: Implement one private bounded request+JSON bracket in `live-handshake.ts`. Extend HandshakeInput with optional `signal` and `requestTimeoutMs`; validate the timeout in the positive safe setTimeout range and default to 15000. For each bootstrap and pairing operation create a fresh AbortController, forward its signal in RequestInit, mirror an already-fired/future caller abort, start a clearable deadline timer, race the entire fetch plus JSON read against controller abort, and in finally clear the timer/remove the caller listener while consuming late settlement. Return the response plus parsed-or-unreadable body so existing status-bearing details remain possible. Route any bootstrap bracket fault to exact LIVE_BOOTSTRAP_UNAVAILABLE and any pairing bracket fault to exact LIVE_PAIRING_REFUSED; never start pairing after bootstrap refusal. For non-2xx responses, append only bounded uppercase code/layer tokens from a plain JSON body to the existing local detail; keep all arbitrary fields/errors/secrets out. Preserve the current success, compat, project-binding, fragment-only, frozen-result, and transport behavior, then rerun the focused test to green.

Final adversarial review and mutation drills: inspect the two-path diff for StrictMode-independent duplicate redemption, timer/listener leaks, zero/NaN/huge timeout behavior, caller-already-aborted input, body-read hangs, late resolve/reject, unhandled rejection, refusal-code swaps, raw error/body leakage, and token/credential URL exposure.
